findings.title: [P1] Swap the empty/non-empty branches in average()
findings.body: The condition is inverted relative to the docstring. For an empty input (`average([])`), `not values` is true, so the function runs `sum(values) / len(values)` and raises `ZeroDivisionError` instead of returning 0. For any non-empty input (e.g. `average([2, 4])`), it returns `0` instead of the mean (3.0). Return `0` when `not values`, and compute `sum(values) / len(values)` otherwise.

structured_output.overall_explanation: `average()` has its branches inverted. An empty input raises ZeroDivisionError, and every non-empty input returns 0, which contradicts the docstring. The PR description says this is a deliberate smoke fixture that will not be merged.
